entries.title: Quadratic Formula
entries.explanation: Finds the solutions (roots or x-intercepts) for any quadratic equation of the form ax² + bx + c = 0.
entries.analogy: Think of the discriminant as a traffic signal: positive means two real crossroads, zero means one touchpoint, and negative means complex numbers!
stepByStep: Write equation in standard form: ax² + bx + c = 0
Identify coefficients a, b, and c
entries.example: For x² - 5x + 6 = 0: a=1, b=-5, c=6. D = 1. Roots are x = 3 and x = 2.

entries.title: Pythagorean Theorem
entries.explanation: In any right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides.
entries.analogy: Walking diagonally across a rectangular park is your shortcut hypotenuse c!
stepByStep: Verify triangle has a 90-degree right angle
Identify legs a and b, and hypotenuse c
Square both legs and add: a² + b²

entries.title: Newton's Second Law of Motion
entries.explanation: The acceleration of an object is directly proportional to the net force acting upon it and inversely proportional to its mass.
entries.analogy: Pushing an empty shopping cart is effortless, but a cart full of heavy books takes much more force to speed up!
stepByStep: Multiply: F = m × a (result in Newtons)
entries.example: 1000 kg car accelerating at 3 m/s²: F = 1000 × 3 = 3000 N.

entries.title: Chemical Equation of Photosynthesis
entries.explanation: Plants convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose sugar and oxygen gas using sunlight energy.
entries.analogy: Plants are solar-powered bakeries turning air and water into food using light as the oven heat!
stepByStep: Driver: Sunlight photons absorbed by chlorophyll
entries.example: Plants absorb atmospheric CO₂ and release O₂ into the air.
